- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overhang.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates future values; cap forecast at 1.2x recent high or use moving average of 3–5 prior days for smoothing.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.27–0.80), model exhibits lagged response; shift forecast horizon 1–2 days forward to align with sentiment momentum.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment <0.3), model underestimates mean reversion; add 2–3% upward bias to forecast to account for rebound toward historical mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture early correction after sharp declines; add a 1–2 day “buffer” of 2–5% upward adjustment to prevent premature bottoming.
